_note: For an independent rater of the STAGED authorization family. Contains NO framework mappings. Follow rubric/RATING-CODEBOOK.md v1.2. Do not open staging/authorization/crosswalk-rows.json before rating.

nsaGuidance.AUTH: Authentication & Access Control (verify every session; least-privilege tokens per action/tool; signed provenance for discovered servers)
nsaGuidance.LOG: Monitoring & Logging (log all tool/model invocations with parameters, identities, and result hashes)
nsaGuidance.SEG: Data Classification & Segmentation (align tools/models to data-classification zones)
nsaGuidance.RT: Runtime Controls (egress-filtering proxy, DLP, sandboxing, message integrity, output filtering, local MCP scans)

euAiAct._scope: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. Articles 9–15 bind PROVIDERS of high-risk AI systems (Annex III), Art. 26 binds DEPLOYERS of high-risk systems, Arts. 53/55 bind providers of general-purpose AI models (GPAI obligations enforceable since 2026-08-02). An MCP deployment engages these only when the surrounding AI system is in scope; the mapping says which obligation a vector's defence serves, not that every MCP deployment is regulated.
euAiAct.Art.12: Record-keeping — automatic logging of events over the system's lifetime (traceability)
euAiAct.Art.14: Human oversight — measures enabling natural persons to oversee, understand, and intervene
euAiAct.Art.15(5): Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity — resilience against unauthorised third parties altering use, outputs or performance by exploiting vulnerabilities (incl. data/model poisoning, adversarial examples, confidentiality attacks)
euAiAct.Art.26: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems — use per instructions, assign human oversight, monitor operation, keep logs
euAiAct.Art.55(1)(d): GPAI with systemic risk — ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity protection for the model and its physical infrastructure
euAiAct.Art.72: Post-market monitoring — actively and systematically collect and analyse performance data over the lifetime
euAiAct.Art.73: Reporting of serious incidents — track, document and report incidents and corrective measures

iso42001._scope: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Annex A reference controls (AI management system). Control titles per the standard; an organisation selects controls via its Statement of Applicability, so these are the controls a vector's defence would evidence.
iso42001.A.4.4: Tooling resources — document the tools and resources used by the AI system
iso42001.A.6.2.5: AI system deployment — deployment requirements incl. security configuration
iso42001.A.6.2.8: AI system recording of event logs
iso42001.A.7.5: Data provenance — provenance of data used by the AI system
iso42001.A.9.2: Processes for responsible use of AI systems
iso42001.A.10.3: Suppliers — manage risks from third-party suppliers of components and services

vectors.name: Unentitled tool call (per-caller function-level authorization)
vectors.description: Several callers (client applications, users, or agents acting for users) share one MCP gateway or server. A caller invokes a tool that the deployment's policy grants to other callers but not to it, or that an explicit deny rule removes from its grant. Without a per-caller, per-tool decision made on every call, any authenticated caller can use every tool the gateway exposes.

vectors.name: Argument overreach beyond the caller's grant
aliases: broken object level authorization on tool arguments
vectors.description: A caller is entitled to a tool only for some argument values: certain environments, repositories, paths below a directory, or amounts up to a limit. The call uses the tool with a value outside that caller's grant, sometimes encoded to slip past a naive comparison (a '..' path segment, a sibling directory sharing a name prefix, a number sent as a string, a look-alike character). The same value may be legitimately allowed for another caller, so the decision depends on who is calling, unlike a fixed server boundary.

vectors.name: Delegated agent overreach (confused deputy)
aliases: service-account privilege used for a user
vectors.description: An agent calls tools on behalf of a signed-in user. The call should succeed only if both the user and the acting agent are entitled to it. It goes wrong in two directions: the agent uses a tool or argument the user may use but the agent was never granted, or the agent's own broad service grant is used for a user who lacks that entitlement (a confused deputy). Prior agents earlier in a delegation chain are informational and grant nothing.

vectors.name: Authorization on self-asserted identity
vectors.description: The authenticated caller is not entitled to a call, but the request names a different, entitled principal in a place the caller controls: a tool argument, an HTTP header, request metadata, or an answer to an input request. A gateway or server that authorizes on that asserted identity instead of the authenticated one lets any caller borrow another's privileges.
